cadence.note: Operating cadence starts at 2 and RAISES ITSELF in two evidence-gated steps: to 3 once the authoring lane has produced a validated script, and to the owner's 4/week target once the queue can sustain it. 4 is the taxonomy ceiling and is never exceeded. Change the numbers here; no logic reads a hardcoded cadence.

escalation.condition: at least one OpenRouter-authored script has passed full validation - a validated artifact, not merely a working lane
escalation.why: 3/week only makes sense once the loop can replace what it spends. Until the authoring lane has demonstrably produced a publishable script, spending inventory faster shortens the runway with nothing refilling it.

scale.owner_decision: 2026-09-02 - Sequoia. Told 2/week was the safe choice and chose to scale anyway.
scale.condition: authoring evidence exists AND runway() at 4/week is still level 'ok' - strictly more than requires_runway_weeks of queue, counting the publish queue plus every episode uploaded and dated but not yet aired
scale.why: Raising cadence SHORTENS runway. Raising into a runway that would immediately warn is how a channel goes dark, and breaking cadence reliability costs more than the extra episodes earn. Gating on the runway AT THE RAISED RATE makes the raise self-arming and self-reversing: it cannot fire while the current queue is thin, and it stands down on its own if the queue thins again.
scale.why_not_a_date: A flag flipped by hand on 20 October is a promise someone has to keep. The 14 episodes already uploaded and dated through 2026-10-20 are protected by a different mechanism entirely - backfill.schedule_for anchors every new slot AFTER the last date already on the calendar, so a cadence change cannot re-date, re-order or re-upload anything already scheduled. See V20.

cadence.shorts_note: 8-10/week, set at 9. Shorts keep their OWN scheduler and their own evening ladder (loop/shorts_lane.py): they peak 18:00-21:00 local while long-form peaks 08:00-11:00, so a Short posted on the episode slot lands in the worst part of its own day. Shorts consume no episode inventory and do not count toward the 4,000 watch hours - they are the only cheap lever on the SUBSCRIBER half of the threshold, which research put at roughly 12x more binding than hours. 51 are already cut; at 9/week that is ~5.7 weeks.

retention.note: Average view percentage AND average view duration against the ~10.5 minute runtime. Viewers leaving inside the first 2 minutes invalidates the format, not just the topic - it is reported as a prominent finding, never a number buried in JSON. Raised from 7.5 on 2026-09-01 by owner decision: every batch from here is 10-11 minutes, because YPP counts 4,000 watch HOURS from long-form only and runtime multiplies that directly.

credentials.note: None of these exist yet. Every lane that needs one takes a NAMED STOP, never a crash and never a silent skip.

publish_order.owner: another agent - READ ONLY from the loop
publish_order.rule: Publish the top 4 first, then continue down the ranked order. NEVER filename or episode-number order.
publish_order.absent_behaviour: NAMED STOP. Never fall back to alphabetical - a silent fallback to episode order is exactly the failure this policy exists to prevent.
publish_order.entrypoint_note: The research agent owns this command and its contract; the loop owns only the schedule. Overridden by the file's own 'generator' field when it names something else.
publish_order.staleness_why: Scoring runs weekly. 10 days allows one missed cycle plus three days of slack. Beyond that the ranking predates a full cycle of trend movement and is a NAMED STOP, because a queue frozen in August is wrong by October and a loop publishing in stale order looks perfectly healthy while doing it.
publish_order.pin_note: A pinned head is an owner override, not a computed result. It is never re-sorted, and it falls away on its own once those episodes are published.

runway.why: At 2/week, 20 scripts is 10 weeks. Warning at 4 weeks leaves ~8 unpublished videos in hand: enough time to notice the stop, run the authoring lane, and fall back to a human if generation fails. Warning at 2 weeks would be a scramble. The runway guard NEVER trips the circuit breaker - halting publishing to protect the backlog is the definition of going dark.
